mainTopic: רבי יוחנן's list of three cases where חכמים followed the majority: why רבי יהושע בן לוי's case is missing, and what kind of case the list is meant to exclude.
overview: Earlier, רבי יוחנן said there are only three cases where חכמים settled a doubt by following the majority and treated it as certain. The amud opens by asking why one more case is missing. רבי יהושע בן לוי ruled that a woman who miscarried in a river brings the birth offerings, because most women give birth to a full baby. The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן's list only counts cases taught in a משנה or ברייתא. It then defends that answer against רבין's report of an objection from the case of a טועה. Next the גמרא asks what kind of case רבי יוחנן's rule is meant to exclude. The case of a רוב opposed by a חזקה is rejected, since רבי יוחנן already ruled on it in the case of the child found next to the dough. The גמרא then suggests the rule excludes the רוב of רבי יהודה, from the משנה of a woman who miscarries a piece of flesh. Finally, שמואל and רבי יוחנן disagree about exactly which piece of flesh רבי יהודה and the חכמים argue about, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A woman who miscarried in the river brings an offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting רבי יהושע בן לוי's ruling. A woman who miscarried in a river brings the birth offerings, and the bird offering is eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: …and she miscarried: she brings an offering, and it is eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote of רבי יהושע בן לוי's ruling, which it uses to challenge רבי יוחנן's list of only three cases. A woman who miscarried in a river, without knowing what she lost, still brings her offering, and it is eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman cannot check whether the fetus was fully formed, so we do not know for sure that she owes a birth offering. Even so, she brings the offering, and the bird חטאת may be eaten as a real קרבן. This treats a doubtful case as certain, which is exactly the kind of case on רבי יוחנן's list.

keyTerms.meaning: She miscarried
An offering; here, the offerings brought by a woman after giving birth
And it is eaten; the bird חטאת is treated as a real offering

phrases.english: and she miscarried —
phrases.notes: We are joining the quote in the middle. The start of the case, a woman crossing a river, came just before this.

phrases.english: she brings an offering, and it is eaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the case that the challenge (begun on the previous daf) brings against רבי יוחנן's list.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's statement that there are only three such cases
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Here is another case where a doubt is treated as certain, so the list seems incomplete.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman who miscarried an unknown fetus in a river brings the birth offerings, and the bird חטאת is eaten.

steps.title: The reason: follow the majority of women
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי explains that we follow the majority of women, and most women give birth to a real, full baby.
steps.simpleTranslation: Follow the majority of women, and most women give birth to a full-fledged baby.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי יהושע בן לוי's reason, which shows this really is a case of following the majority. That strengthens the question of why רבי יוחנן left it off his list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since most pregnant women give birth to a real, fully formed baby, we assume this woman did too, even though we cannot check. This is a doubt settled by רוב, and it involves a woman's status after birth. So it fits the pattern of רבי יוחנן's cases, and the challenge gets sharper.

keyTerms.meaning: The majority; following what usually happens
A proper, full-fledged baby
A doubt; a case where the facts are unknown

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a majority rule can be strong enough to require a real קרבן and to let it be eaten.

phrases.english: Follow the majority of women,
and most women give birth to a full-fledged offspring.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind the ruling in step 1, showing that it rests on רוב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's count of only three cases
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This ruling is clearly based on the majority in a case of doubt, so it should have been counted.

steps.title: The list only counts cases from a משנה or ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן listed only cases taught in a משנה or ברייתא. He did not include rulings of אמוראים like רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are speaking of a משנה; we are not speaking of a later ruling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. רבי יוחנן's list only included cases from a משנה or ברייתא, and this case comes from an אמורא's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed the list was meant to cover every case of this kind. The answer narrows the list: it only covers cases found in the teachings of the תנאים. Since this case is a ruling of רבי יהושע בן לוי, its absence is no problem.

keyTerms.meaning: A משנה; here it includes a ברייתא too, meaning a teaching of the תנאים
A teaching or ruling of an אמורא

steps.confusionAlert: The answer does not say רבי יהושע בן לוי is wrong. It only says his ruling was not the kind of source רבי יוחנן was listing.

phrases.english: We are speaking of a Mishna;
phrases.notes: Here this means any teaching of the תנאים, so a ברייתא counts too.

phrases.english: we are not speaking of an amoraic ruling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from steps 1 and 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the original list
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן's list should include every case where a doubt was settled by the majority.
steps.terutzMaskana: The list only includes cases from a משנה or ברייתא, so an אמורא's ruling is not counted.

steps.title: רבין reports an objection from the case of an unsure woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the answer by quoting רבין. He reported that רבי יוסי בר רבי חנינא raised an objection against רבי יהושע בן לוי from the case of a טועה, but רבין did not know what the objection was.
steps.simpleTranslation: But when רבין came, he said: רבי יוסי בר רבי חנינא raised an objection from the case of an unsure woman, and I do not know what his objection was.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on its own answer by quoting רבין's report. This sets up the next part of the discussion, which will try to work out what the objection was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי בר רבי חנינא challenged רבי יהושע בן לוי's ruling using a teaching about a טועה, a woman unsure about her birth. This shows that the topic is tied to an older teaching, which raises a question about the answer in step 3. רבין himself did not know the content of the objection, so the גמרא will need to figure it out.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who is unsure; here, one who does not know when she gave birth
A strong objection or refutation
And I do not know

phrases.english: But when Ravin came, he said:

phrases.aramaic: מֵתִיב רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא טוֹעָה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Rabbi Ḥanina raises an objection from the case of an unsure woman,
phrases.notes: This is a woman who does not know when she gave birth.

phrases.english: and I do not know what his objection is.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 3 by bringing in an objection to רבי יהושע בן לוי's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that רבי יהושע בן לוי's case is only an amoraic ruling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An objection from the teaching about a טועה shows that the case is tied to an older source, so the answer in step 3 is called into question.

steps.title: Maybe the ברייתא actually supports רבי יהושע בן לוי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבין meant the ברייתא of the טועה is not a refutation but a support for רבי יהושע בן לוי. If so, his ruling has a ברייתא source, and רבי יוחנן should have listed it.
steps.simpleTranslation: What, doesn't this mean it is not a refutation, but rather a support?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is reading רבין's report as hinting that the ברייתא backs up רבי יהושע בן לוי. That would bring back the problem of why רבי יוחנן left the case off his list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answer (step 3) said רבי יוחנן listed only rulings found in a משנה or ברייתא. If the ברייתא of the טועה supports רבי יהושע בן לוי, then his ruling is taught in a ברייתא too. That breaks the earlier answer.

keyTerms.meaning: What, isn't it...? A way of offering an interpretation as the obvious one
A refutation, a strong objection that knocks down a view
Support, a source that backs up a view

phrases.english: What, is it not that it is not a refutation,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the ברייתא about the טועה that רבין mentioned in the last step.

phrases.english: but rather a support?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי לָאו לָא תְּיוּבְתָּא, אֶלָּא סִיַּיעְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבין's report from step 4 to challenge the answer of step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 3 that רבי יוחנן listed only cases taught in a משנה or ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the ברייתא supports רבי יהושע בן לוי, his ruling is effectively taught in a ברייתא, so רבי יוחנן should have included it.

steps.title: The ברייתא may be neither a refutation nor a support
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects that reading. Perhaps רבין meant the ברייתא neither disproves nor proves רבי יהושע בן לוי's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, perhaps it is neither a refutation nor a support.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back and says רבין's words don't have to mean the ברייתא supports רבי יהושע בן לוי. It may simply have no bearing either way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא does not support him, then his ruling still has no משנה or ברייתא source. So the answer of step 3 stands: רבי יוחנן did not list it because it is only an אמורא's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps, introduces another possible reading
Neither a refutation nor a support, a source that says nothing about the view

steps.whatToRemember: The answer of step 3 survives: רבי יהושע בן לוי's ruling is not clearly taught in a ברייתא, so רבי יוחנן did not need to list it.

phrases.english: No, perhaps
it is neither a refutation nor a support.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, דִּלְמָא לָא תְּיוּבְתָּא וְלֹא סִיַּיעְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5 by rejecting its reading of רבין.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejecting the inference; offering another possible reading of רבין's words
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבין meant the ברייתא supports רבי יהושע בן לוי, so his ruling has a ברייתא source.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבין may have meant the ברייתא is neutral, so the ruling still has no ברייתא source and רבי יוחנן rightly left it out.

steps.title: What does רבי יוחנן's rule mean to exclude?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new question about רבי יוחנן's statement that in three places חכמים treated an uncertain case as certain: what other kind of case is he leaving out?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It asks what kind of case רבי יוחנן's statement is meant to leave out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By saying that in these three places a doubt is treated as certain, רבי יוחנן implies that in some other case it is not. The גמרא wants to know which case that is.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude, to leave a certain case out of a rule
To exclude what? Asks which case a statement is meant to leave out

phrases.english: To exclude what?
phrases.notes: This goes back to רבי יוחנן's rule that in three places חכמים treated a doubt as if it were certain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion about רבי יהושע בן לוי and returns to the wording of רבי יוחנן's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which type of uncertain case רבי יוחנן's rule of three places is meant to exclude.

steps.title: First suggestion: a majority with a חזקה against it, but רבי יוחנן already said that
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the excluded case is a majority opposed by a חזקה, where we do not burn תרומה. It rejects this because רבי יוחנן already taught that rule another time.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is to exclude a majority that has a חזקה with it, so that we do not burn תרומה because of it, but רבי יוחנן already said that once!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer: the rule excludes a case where a majority points one way but a חזקה points the other way. Then it immediately knocks this down because רבי יוחנן already said it elsewhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that kind of case the doubt is not treated as certain, so תרומה that touched it is not burned. But רבי יוחנן already stated this in a different place, so he would not need to hint at it again here. The search for what he excludes goes on.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say, introduces a suggested answer that will be tested
A majority, the usual case that we follow
Presumptive status, assuming things stay as they were
We burn
The כהן's portion of produce, which must be burned if definitely impure
One time, on another occasion

steps.confusionAlert: Here the רוב and the חזקה pull in opposite directions. The words 'with it' (בַּהֲדֵיהּ) mean 'alongside it in the case', not 'agreeing with it'.

phrases.english: If we say it is to exclude a majority
that has a presumptive status along with it,
phrases.notes: The חזקה here points the other way, against the majority.

phrases.english: so that we do not burn תרומה because of it —
but רבי יוחנן already said it
one time!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא לְמַעוֹטֵי רוּבָּא, דְּאִיכָּא חֲזָקָה בַּהֲדֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers and rejects a first answer to the question of step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רבי יוחנן's rule excludes a majority opposed by a חזקה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן already taught that rule elsewhere, so it is not needed here.

steps.title: The משנה of the child next to the dough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: a child is found beside pure dough with a piece of dough in his hand. רבי מאיר says the dough is pure, and חכמים say it is impure because children tend to touch things.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: A child is found next to dough, and he has some dough in his hand. רבי מאיר says the dough is pure. חכמים say it is impure, because a child usually touches things.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its proof that רבי יוחנן already taught the rule of a רוב against a חזקה. First it quotes the משנה that the discussion is based on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dough was pure, but now we suspect the impure child touched it. רבי מאיר keeps it pure. חכמים call it impure because children normally handle what is near them. This משנה is the base case for רבי יוחנן's earlier ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Dough, here pure dough that has not yet risen
Risen dough; a piece of it is in the child's hand
To touch or handle things
Rules it pure / rule it impure

phrases.english: As we learned in a משנה: A child who is found next to the dough,
and there is dough in his hand,
רבי מאיר rules it pure,
and the Sages rule it impure,
because a child usually touches things.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for Step 8's claim that רבי יוחנן already taught the rule of a רוב opposed by a חזקה.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוחנן already ruled on a רוב opposed by a חזקה
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in טהרות about the child found beside the dough

steps.title: Why רבי מאיר rules the dough pure
steps.stepSummary: Most children touch things, but a minority do not. The dough has a חזקה of being pure. רבי מאיר joins the minority to the חזקה, and this weakens the majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we said: What is רבי מאיר's reason? He holds that most children touch things and a few do not. This dough is still presumed pure. So we join the minority to the presumption, and the majority is weakened.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי מאיר's reasoning in the משנה. It shows that this is a case of a majority against a presumption.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two forces pull in opposite directions. The majority of children handle things, which says the dough became impure. The dough's חזקה of purity says it stayed pure. רבי מאיר adds the minority of children who do not touch things to the חזקה, so the majority loses its strength.

keyTerms.meaning: Majority
Minority
Presumption that something keeps its earlier status
Join the minority to the presumption
Was weakened

phrases.english: And we said: What is רבי מאיר's reason?
He holds: most children touch things,
and a minority do not touch things,
and this dough stands with a presumption of being pure,
so join the minority to the presumption,
and the majority is weakened.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains רבי מאיר's ruling from the משנה in Step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the reason for רבי מאיר's ruling of purity?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The minority joins the חזקה of purity, so the majority is weakened.

steps.title: Why the רבנן rule the dough impure
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן say a minority counts as if it does not exist. That leaves a plain majority against a חזקה, and the majority wins.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן say the minority counts as if it isn't there. So it is a majority against a presumption, and the majority is stronger.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other side: the reasoning of the רבנן in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן do not let the minority add any weight. Once the minority is ignored, it is simply רוב against חזקה. For them, רוב is stronger, so the dough is impure.

keyTerms.meaning: Is treated as if it does not exist
Is stronger and wins out

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say: the minority is treated as if it does not exist,
and between a majority and a presumption, the majority is stronger.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning of the רבנן, against רבי מאיר's reasoning in Step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The minority is ignored, and a רוב beats a חזקה.

steps.title: ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן argue about burning the תרומה
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש, quoting רבי אושעיא, says this is a חזקה strong enough to burn תרומה. רבי יוחנן says it is not. So רבי יוחנן already taught that when a רוב is opposed by a חזקה, תרומה is not burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ריש לקיש said in the name of רבי אושעיא: This is a presumption on which we burn תרומה. And רבי יוחנן said: This is not a presumption on which we burn תרומה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes the proof. רבי יוחנן already ruled that in this case of רוב against חזקה the תרומה is not burned, so he had no need to list it again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even following the רבנן, who say the dough is impure, רבי יוחנן holds the doubt is not strong enough to burn תרומה. The תרומה is left alone: it may not be eaten and may not be burned. Because he already taught this here, his rule of three places (Step 7) cannot be coming to exclude this case.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion given to a כהן; if it is definitely impure, it must be burned
We burn it

steps.confusionAlert: Here the word חזקה refers to the 'presumption' that children touch things, which is really the majority. It does not mean the dough's own חזקה of purity.
steps.whatToRemember: Step 8's suggestion is rejected because רבי יוחנן already taught elsewhere that a רוב opposed by a חזקה does not allow burning תרומה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why רבי יוחנן's 'three places' cannot be meant to exclude the case of a רוב against a חזקה. The next step offers a different answer to the question from Step 7.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא:
phrases.english: And ריש לקיש said in the name of רבי אושעיא:

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ הִיא חֲזָקָה שֶׁשּׂוֹרְפִין עָלֶיהָ אֶת הַתְּרוּמָה,
phrases.english: This is a presumption on which we burn the תרומה,
and רבי יוחנן said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין זוֹ חֲזָקָה שֶׁשּׂוֹרְפִין עָלֶיהָ אֶת הַתְּרוּמָה!
phrases.english: This is not a presumption on which we burn the תרומה!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the משנה and its explanation to show that רבי יוחנן already ruled on רוב against חזקה, which completes Step 8's rejection.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוחנן already taught that a רוב opposed by a חזקה does not allow burning תרומה, so this cannot be what his three places exclude.

steps.title: A new suggestion: the rule excludes רבי יהודה's majority
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops its earlier suggestion. It now proposes that רבי יוחנן's rule is meant to exclude the רוב of רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the rule is meant to exclude the majority of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The earlier suggestion failed, so the גמרא offers a new answer to what רבי יוחנן's rule excludes. This line sets up the next move: quoting the משנה where רבי יהודה's view appears.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case of a רוב against a חזקה was rejected because רבי יוחנן already taught it elsewhere. So the גמרא looks for a different kind of רוב that the rule could be excluding. It points to a רוב that comes from רבי יהודה's opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals that the earlier idea is dropped and a new one is coming.
To exclude a case from a rule
A majority. A ruling based on what usually happens.

phrases.english: Rather, it comes to exclude
the majority of רבי יהודה,
phrases.notes: This means a case where רבי יהודה rules based on a majority. The גמרא is about to show us which case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new answer to step 7's question (what רבי יוחנן's rule excludes), replacing the suggestion rejected in steps 8–12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New identification of the excluded case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule excludes a רוב that is opposed by a חזקה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule excludes the רוב of רבי יהודה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוחנן's rule of three places is meant to exclude the רוב of רבי יהודה.

steps.title: The משנה of the woman who miscarries a piece of flesh
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה. A woman who miscarries a piece of flesh is impure if blood came with it and pure if not. רבי יהודה says she is impure either way.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: a woman who miscarries a piece of flesh is impure if there is blood with it. If there is no blood, she is pure. רבי יהודה says: either way, she is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה that shows the 'majority of רבי יהודה' it just mentioned. In this case, רבי יהודה makes her impure even when no blood is seen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים go by what we see: if there is blood she is impure, and if not she is pure. רבי יהודה makes her impure even without visible blood. That means he assumes blood came out even though nobody saw it. The גמרא will build on this assumption as the 'רוב' that רבי יוחנן's rule excludes.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who miscarries
A shapeless piece of flesh
Ritually impure. Here it means the impurity of a נדה.
Ritually pure
Either way. In both cases.

steps.confusionAlert: The impurity here is the impurity of a נדה, which comes from blood. It is not the impurity of a woman after childbirth. That is why the whole question is whether blood came out with the piece.

phrases.english: As we learned in a משנה: a woman who miscarries a piece of flesh —
if there is blood with it, she is impure,
and if not, she is pure.
רבי יהודה says:
either way, she is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the 'majority of רבי יהודה' mentioned in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: The identity of the 'רוב of רבי יהודה'
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of המפלת חתיכה, where רבי יהודה rules she is impure even without visible blood

steps.title: שמואל limits רבי יהודה's ruling to a piece with the color of impure blood
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל. רבי יהודה made the woman impure only when the piece has the color of one of the four impure kinds of blood. With other colors, she is pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: רבי יהודה made her impure only when the piece has the color of one of the four kinds of impure blood. But if it has the color of other kinds of blood, she is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל explains the limits of רבי יהודה's opinion in the משנה. רבי יהודה does not make her impure for every piece of flesh, only for a piece with an impure blood color.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה made it sound like רבי יהודה says 'impure either way' for every piece. שמואל narrows this: רבי יהודה's ruling applies only when the piece looks like one of the four impure blood colors. If the piece has another color, even רבי יהודה agrees she is pure.

keyTerms.meaning: Ruled impure
The four kinds of blood color that make a woman impure
Other blood colors, which do not make her impure

phrases.english: And רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל:
רבי יהודה ruled her impure

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא בַּחֲתִיכָה שֶׁל אַרְבַּע מִינֵי דָמִים,
phrases.english: only for a piece with the color of the four kinds of blood,
but with other kinds of blood, she is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the exact case where רבי יהודה rules impure in the משנה from step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה rules her impure only for a piece with the color of the four impure blood types. With other colors, she is pure.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן says both clear cases are agreed, and the argument is elsewhere
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that if the piece has an impure blood color, everyone agrees she is impure. If it has another color, everyone agrees she is pure. The argument is only about a different case, which begins to be described here.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: a piece with the color of the four kinds of blood makes her impure according to everyone. A piece with the color of other kinds of blood leaves her pure according to everyone. They disagree only when she miscarried…
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן disagrees with שמואל about where the argument in the משנה lies. He says both of שמואל's cases are actually agreed by everyone. Then he starts to explain the one case they do argue about, and the sentence continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to שמואל, the impure-color piece is exactly where רבי יהודה and the חכמים argue. רבי יוחנן says that even the חכמים agree she is impure in that case, and in the other-color case everyone agrees she is pure. So the real argument must be about some third kind of piece, which the גמרא describes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees. Both sides of the argument hold this.
They disagreed only about…
When she miscarried

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two אמוראים. For שמואל, the impure-color piece is where רבי יהודה argues. For רבי יוחנן, that same case is one that everyone agrees on.

phrases.english: And רבי יוחנן said:
a piece with the color of the four kinds of blood —
everyone agrees she is impure,
and a piece with the color of other blood —
everyone agrees she is pure.
They disagreed only when she miscarried

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different view from שמואל's in step 15 about where the argument in the משנה lies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An impure-color piece makes her impure according to everyone. An other-color piece leaves her pure according to everyone. The argument is only about a different kind of miscarriage.
